grades.quote: The file’s inode and the disk space holding its content are only freed when the file’s link count is zero and no file descriptors refer to it.
grades.reason: Explains that unlink only removes a name. The inode and content are freed only when the link count is zero and no file descriptors refer to it. So the file stays accessible through another link (b) or an open fd.

grades.quote: is an idiomatic way to create a temporary inode with no name that will be cleaned up when the process closes fd or exits.
grades.reason: Gives the open-then-unlink idiom. The unnamed inode persists until the fd is closed or the process exits. This shows the open-fd case, but it doesn't spell out the reading or the link-count rule.

grades.quote: The operating system removes the file when it no longer has any names and is no longer in use by any process. (An open file can continue to exist without any names, as you can demonstrate in Exploration Project 8.10.)
grades.reason: States that unlink removes only a name. The file is removed only when it has no names and no process is using it, and an open file can continue to exist without names. This directly explains why it can still be read.
Only introduces symbolic links as another way to reach a file by multiple names. It says nothing about unlink or reading a file after unlink.
